author: hattrill
body:
I asked Claude pro and the response aligns with the conclusion I came to independently. 
"DIS3L2 is better characterized as a cytoplasmic RNA surveillance factor rather than a core P-body component.
Key points:
Against core P-body residency:

DIS3L2 is a 3′→5′ processive exonuclease (belongs to the RNase II/RNB family) that acts on oligouridylated RNA substrates in the cytoplasm — its activity is upstream of or parallel to P-body-associated decay
It lacks the canonical interaction domains (like the FFD motif, IDRs driving condensation, or Lsm-interaction surfaces) that scaffold P-body assembly
The TUTase→DIS3L2 pathway (ZCCHC6/TUT7 oligouridylating substrates like pre-let-7, histone mRNAs, damaged rRNA) is generally described as operating in the bulk cytoplasm

The nuance:

Some proteomics studies of P-body-enriched fractions have detected DIS3L2, but this is difficult to interpret cleanly — proximity to P-bodies doesn't equal residency, and cytoplasmic decay factors often co-purify
There is a conceptual question of whether substrates handed off from TUTases get degraded before or after P-body association

Bottom line: DIS3L2 is most accurately described as a cytoplasmic exonuclease whose substrates and activity intersect with P-body-regulated RNA metabolism, but it lacks the hallmarks of a bona fide P-body constituent. It's in a similar position to the exosome — cytoplasmic decay machinery that interfaces with mRNA fate decisions but isn't a P-body scaffolding component."
